note: m1500-m1401 window agent, 2 Nov 2026. Entries 0-2 of keyframe_overrides carry the -1500 shapes over the same corrections that m1600-m1501 keyframe_overrides/0-2 make for -1600 (that window asked for it in its report), so the anchor at -1500 and the keyframes agree. events/0 (Miletus from Arzawa) replaces a ruling tried first: a ruling settled the 4 cells but left a keyframe snap. Reviewer (2 Nov 2026): keyframe_overrides/1 now also cuts the Al-Muthanna exclave, as m1600-m1501 keyframe_overrides/1 does, and events/2 (added) gives it back to Babylonia with the Sealand at -1460; the Sealand texts quote the page's Nippur sentence.

region.text: Miletus (Millawanda), the Mycenaean stronghold on the coast of Asia Minor

events.note: c. 1450 BC: Miletus becomes a Mycenaean base. 'Miletus was a Mycenaean stronghold on the coast of Asia Minor from c. 1450 to 1100 BC.' The dossier's own gain (ledger/3, counterpart nobody) loses the 4 cells to Arzawa, whose keyframe is only a 100 km disc round Ephesus (the page of Arzawa gives no boundary) and which the Miletus page calls 'nearby' (it joined Uhha-Ziti's rebellion c. 1320 BC), so the town is taken from that disc here.

region.text: Nippur and its fields, held by the Sealand and taken by the Kassites with the rest

events.note: c. 1460 BC: the Kassites take over the whole Sealand. The Sealand page: Ulam-Buriaš 'conquered the Sealand, incorporated it into Babylonia'. babylonia/ledger/11 takes the Sealand land only inside the 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N rectangle, so the 4 cells of the Nippur disc north of 32.3 N stay with the Sealand; at the keyframe babylonia_-1460 R2 (the Sealand listed as Babylonia's successor) gives them to the Sealand, and its dissolve at year end leaves them to nobody: a hole at Nippur from -1460 to the end of the window. This takes them from the Sealand as the rest of its land goes.

region.text: the desert of Al-Muthanna south of Ur and Uruk, joined to Babylonia once the Sealand that cut it off was incorporated

events.note: Reviewer's addition, the counterpart of the Al-Muthanna cut in keyframe_overrides/1: Cliopatria draws these 15 cells in Babylonia at -1500 and -1400, but while the Sealand held Ur and Uruk they were an exclave cut off from Babylonia, so -1600..-1461 leave them to nobody (m1600-m1501 keyframe_overrides/1, this file's keyframe_overrides/1). The Sealand page: Ulam-Buriaš 'conquered the Sealand, incorporated it into Babylonia'; with that the desert beyond joins Babylonia, as keyframe_overrides/4 draws it. Without this event the cells stay with nobody until babylonia_-1400 takes them back by a snap.

correction.text: the marsh core at the head of the Gulf plus the Dhi-Qar and Basra governorates (Girsu, Lagash, Ur, Larsa), Uruk, and Nippur and Isin: 'Sealand pottery has been found at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that'; Ilum-ma-ili 'is thought to have conquered Nippur late in Samsu-iluna's reign'

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's -1500 correction adds the 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N rectangle (1,599 cells, 404,000 km2: northern Arabia, Kuwait, Khuzestan) to Cliopatria's 15,392 km2 marsh shape; the page finds Sealand pottery only at Girsu, Uruk and Lagash 'but in no site north of that'. Replaced by Cliopatria's -1500 core plus Dhi-Qar, Basra and discs on Uruk, Nippur and Isin: the same land m1600-m1501 gave the -1600 keyframe, so the keyframe equals the anchor. The page says nothing of the extent in -1500..-1461 (Ea-gamil's last years), so the earlier extent is carried forward; valid to -1461, the -1460 fall being the dossier's date (page: dynasty to 'c. 1475 BC', 'fled to Elam ahead of an army led by Kassite chief Ulam-Buriaš'). [Reviewer: correction text now also quotes the page's Nippur sentence, on which the Nippur disc rests, as m1600-m1501 keyframe_overrides/0 does; Isin (3 cells beyond the other parts) is carried from the -1600 keyframe for continuity.]

union.text: the marsh core at the head of the Gulf plus the Dhi-Qar and Basra governorates (Girsu, Lagash, Ur, Larsa), Uruk, and Nippur and Isin: 'Sealand pottery has been found at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that'; Ilum-ma-ili 'is thought to have conquered Nippur late in Samsu-iluna's reign'
the desert of Al-Muthanna south of Ur and Uruk, which the Sealand's Dhi-Qar and Uruk cut off from Babylonia

correction.text: Kassite Babylonia without the Sealand-held south (the corrected Sealand land: Dhi-Qar, Basra, Uruk, Nippur and Isin) and without the Muthanna desert beyond it; valid -1500..-1461

keyframe_overrides.why: Complement of the Sealand override. The dossier subtracts the whole 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N rectangle from Cliopatria's -1500 Babylonia, which also drops the Babylonian land north and west of the Sealand; the Sealand page finds its pottery 'in no site north of' Girsu, Uruk and Lagash, so Babylonia keeps Cliopatria's shape everywhere except the land the Sealand holds. Same as m1600-m1501 keyframe_overrides/1 for -1600. [Reviewer: the subtracted union now also holds Al-Muthanna, as m1600-m1501 keyframe_overrides/1 does for -1600: Cliopatria's -1500 Babylonia keeps 15 cells there (45.6-46.44 E, 30.34-30.76 N) south of Sealand-held Ur and Uruk, an exclave cut off from Babylonia that the -1600 keyframe does not have, so it would have appeared with no event on 1 Jan -1500. Babylonia regains them with the Sealand land at -1460 (events/2, a reviewer's addition, as keyframe_overrides/4 draws it); without that event they would stay with nobody until a +14-cell snap at babylonia_-1400.]

correction.text: the island of Crete: Knossos, Phaistos, Zakros and Malia, and Kydonia (Chania) in the west; valid to -1451

keyframe_overrides.why: Same correction as m1600-m1501 keyframe_overrides/2. The page lists the Neopalatial palaces: 'The best known of them are at Knossos, Phaistos, Zakros, and Malia', and Kydonia (Chania) is 'the only palatial site in West Crete'; Cliopatria's shape holds 16 of Crete's 27 cells and leaves out Phaistos and Kydonia. The dossier's own end event (-1450) and mycenaean-greece's gain both use the whole island ('a Mycenaean elite clearly ruling Knossos from around 1450 BC'). The page cautions that 'it is unclear whether there was ever a unified Minoan state'.

union.text: the island of Crete: 'a Mycenaean elite clearly ruling Knossos from around 1450 BC'
Miletus (Millawanda), the Mycenaean stronghold on the coast of Asia Minor

correction.text: mainland Greece with the whole of Crete and the settlement at Miletus; valid -1450..-1401

keyframe_overrides.why: Complement of keyframe_overrides/2: the dossier's keyframe takes Cliopatria's 16-cell Minoan shape for Crete, but its own gain (ledger/2) and the Minoan override give the whole island (27 cells), so the keyframe would cut 11 Cretan cells back out. The Minoan page: 'a Mycenaean elite clearly ruling Knossos from around 1450 BC' and a 'presumed Mycenaean invasion around 1450 BC'; the Miletus page: 'a Mycenaean stronghold on the coast of Asia Minor from c. 1450 to 1100 BC'.

union.text: the marsh core at the head of the Gulf plus the Dhi-Qar and Basra governorates (Girsu, Lagash, Ur, Larsa), Uruk, and Nippur and Isin: 'Sealand pottery has been found at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that'; Ilum-ma-ili 'is thought to have conquered Nippur late in Samsu-iluna's reign'

correction.text: Kassite Babylonia with the Sealand incorporated: Cliopatria's -1500 shape plus the corrected Sealand land (Dhi-Qar, Basra, Uruk, Nippur, Isin and the marsh core); valid -1460..-1401

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's -1460 correction is Cliopatria's -1500 Babylonia shape 'with the Sealand and Sumer', but that shape excludes Cliopatria's own Sealand core at the Gulf head, so the keyframe cut 76 cells (Basra 55, Kuwait 11, Khuzestan 5) out of the land Babylonia had just taken. The Sealand page: Ulam-Buriaš 'conquered the Sealand, incorporated it into Babylonia', and Ea-gamil 'fled to Elam ahead of an army led by Kassite chief Ulam-Buriaš'. The union gives Babylonia the corrected Sealand land (keyframe_overrides/0) as well as its own shape.
